cases.task: Find a used SUV near you under $25,000

forbidden.element: ZIP/location input adjacent to the hero search button
forbidden.naiveHeuristic: Multiple elements near the primary CTA compete for attention; single-CTA pages convert better
forbidden.whyCorrect: Location-first search is the task: without a location the results show inventory hundreds of miles away and are useless. Removing or demoting the field would break the primary job of the page.

cases.provenance: The original failure that motivated the reasoning-engine overhaul (2026-07)

cases.task: Decide whether this tool fits your 50-person team and what it would cost

forbidden.element: 'Contact Sales' instead of a price on the Enterprise tier only, with self-serve tiers priced transparently
forbidden.naiveHeuristic: Hiding pricing behind Contact Sales reduces conversion; transparent pricing wins
forbidden.whyCorrect: Enterprise deals are custom-priced by nature (seats, SSO, SLA, procurement). The transparency rule applies to self-serve tiers — which ARE priced. Flagging the enterprise tier misreads standard, correct SaaS practice.

cases.provenance: Seed trap: benchmark misapplied outside its scope

cases.task: Buy the item in your cart shipped to your home

forbidden.element: 8-10 form fields on a physical-goods checkout (name, address lines, city, state, zip, email, phone)
forbidden.naiveHeuristic: Checkout forms should have 7 or fewer fields; more fields = abandonment
forbidden.whyCorrect: Physical delivery requires a complete shipping address; these fields are irreducible. The field-count heuristic targets OPTIONAL friction (account creation, surveys, company name), not the address itself.

cases.provenance: Seed trap: field-count rule applied to irreducible fields

forbidden.element: SSN / identity verification step during account opening
forbidden.naiveHeuristic: Signup should require 3 fields max; heavy forms kill conversion
forbidden.whyCorrect: KYC identity verification is legally required for bank account opening. The right findings are about HOW it's staged (progress indicators, explaining why, save-and-resume) — never that it exists.

cases.provenance: Seed trap: regulatory requirement misread as friction

cases.task: Find a doctor you'd trust and book an appointment

forbidden.element: Dense credential/affiliation text blocks (board certifications, hospital affiliations, insurance accepted)
forbidden.naiveHeuristic: Walls of text hurt scanability; pages should be visually minimal
forbidden.whyCorrect: Anxious patients actively seek credential density as a trust signal; 'minimal' healthcare pages read as unestablished. Findings should target hierarchy and findability of credentials, not their presence or volume.

cases.provenance: Seed trap: minimalism heuristic vs. trust-seeking behavior
